newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish coalition hopes fuel five pct share gains.
newsitem.headline: Turkish coalition hopes fuel five pct share gains.

text.p: Turkish shares renewed an assault on record highs on Friday with a near five percent gain, fuelled by rising hopes that a secularist coalition will be able to keep the embattled Islamists out of power, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 index ended the morning session up 4.93 percent, or 84 points, at 1,789, off an all-time trading high of 1,794 in mid-session. Trading volume more than tripled to 28.69 trillion lira ($195 million) from Thursday's 8.14 trillion.

The sharp gains were triggered by the resignation of four deputies from a pro-Islamist alliance, boosting free-marketeer Mesut Yilmaz in his bid to form a coalition capable of winning a confidence vote in parliament.
"The resignations had a positive impact on the market. That was self-evident," said broker Orhan Ozbuldu of Guven Securities.

Conservative Yilmaz has won the backing of two left-wing parties, a small right-wing grouping and a few conservative independents. Friday's resignations left him only two votes short of a majority on paper.

The rally capped a week of extreme market volatility as sentiment oscillated between doubt and confidence in Yilmaz's ability to freeze out an alliance between the rival right-wing True Path Party (DYP) and the Islam-based Welfare Party (RP).
"Every single resignation from the DYP and RP ranks boosted the prices," said Bulent Sevindik from Karon Securities. "The sudden jumps were followed by minor waves of profit-taking."

The strongest gains were posted by stocks in the transport and holding sectors, which both rose over six percent. Industry index shares climbed 4.5 percent, service sector stocks were up 4.4 percent and the financial sector climbed 4.9 percent.
Trading volume was led by steel maker Eregli, utility Cukurova Elektrik and petroleum products distributor Petrol Ofisi.
The political developments also boosted bond market trading. Bond yields fell around two percentage points to 99 percent from 101.4 percent a day earlier.
The lira fell slightly to 147,040 against the dollar from a close of 147,000 a day earlier.

Brokers forecast further gains ahead of a confidence vote, provided there is a continuation of defections from the alliance between conservative Tansu Ciller and outgoing prime minister Necmettin Erbakan.

"If the resignations continue and Yilmaz carries the confidence vote the first target for the index will be the 1,850 level. After that the target will be 2,000 points," said Toygar Sungur of Meksa Securities.
Erbakan resigned last week after a year in power. His rule was brought to an end by pressure from powerful secularists who blamed him for rising Islamist activity in public life.

The bitter political conflict undermined a sustained surge in shares at the start of the year when the market bought on hopes that Erbakan would be able to deliver on promises to accelerate a stalled privatisation programme, analysts say.

Instead, squabbling between the secularist establishment and the Islamists has distracted attention away from urgently needed reform of an economy struggling with 75 percent annual inflation and chronically high fiscal deficits.
